name: 1 & 2 Peter: Suffering, Holiness, and False Teachers
path: New Testament Studies: Life and Doctrine in Christ

objectives.text: Identify Peter as the disciple who denied Jesus three times and was restored by Jesus to care for his sheep
Name Peter's picture of believers as living stones built on Jesus the cornerstone
Recall Peter's teaching that suffering for doing good is blessed because Jesus suffered for us and left an example
Describe Peter's instruction to cast all anxieties on God because he cares for his people
Describe Peter's picture of the devil as a roaring lion and his call to be watchful and resist him firm in the faith
Summarize the living hope and imperishable inheritance that Peter says believers have through the resurrection of Jesus
Explain the command to be holy because God is holy and trace it back to its source in Leviticus
Explain how Peter describes believers as ransomed by the precious blood of Christ who bore their sins
Compare temporary trials with eternal glory using Peter's image of faith refined like gold
List the qualities Peter tells believers to add to their faith and explain how God's promises supply what is needed for godliness
Identify the marks of false teachers described in 2 Peter such as denying the Master, greed, and sensuality
Explain how Peter applies Israel's titles of royal priesthood and holy nation to the church
Analyze Peter's description of believers as exiles and sojourners and how it shapes their conduct among unbelievers
Prepare a respectful answer for the hope Christians hold, following Peter's instruction to speak with gentleness and a good conscience
Interpret Peter's explanation of the apparent delay of the Lord's return as God's patience toward sinners
Explain how Peter connects Noah's rescue through the flood to baptism as a sign rather than a mere outward washing
Explain how Peter uses his eyewitness account of the transfiguration to show that the apostolic message is not a cleverly devised myth
Explain how Peter's examples of the flood, Sodom, Noah, and Lot show both God's judgment on the wicked and his rescue of the godly
Analyze how 1 Peter presents Christ's suffering as both a substitutionary atonement and an example for believers, drawing on Isaiah 53
Construct a summary of the theology of suffering taught across 1 Peter
Evaluate Peter's call to submission to civil rulers, masters, and husbands in light of its stated purposes and its limits elsewhere in Scripture
Defend the Reformed doctrine of the inspiration of Scripture using Peter's teaching on prophets carried along by the Spirit and his recognition of Paul's letters as Scripture
Analyze Peter's teaching on the day of the Lord and the new heavens and new earth, including how translation choices affect its reading
Compare the main interpretations of Christ preaching to the spirits in prison and evaluate them against the context of 1 Peter
Evaluate scholarly arguments about the authorship and date of 2 Peter in light of the letter's own claims
Analyze Peter's charge to elders to shepherd the flock under the Chief Shepherd and relate it to his own restoration by Jesus

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (Peter's restoration, living stones, blessed suffering, roaring lion, living hope, holiness, trials and glory, false teachers, exiles, delay of return, Noah and baptism, transfiguration, theology of suffering, submission, inspiration) and anchored each to specific verses. Replaced the vague 'pastoral heart' synthesis with an analysis of Peter's charge to elders. Added missing competencies: casting anxieties on God, ransom by Christ's blood, the virtues of 2 Peter 1, royal priesthood, giving a reason for hope, judgment and rescue in 2 Peter 2, Christ's suffering as atonement and example, the new heavens and earth, the spirits in prison, and authorship of 2 Peter. Left Jude's parallel material on false teachers to the Jude sub-topic.
